hidden-past-berlin.description:

ai-tested-honesty.title: Will AI Say “I Don't Know”? We Tested Models on Made-Up Products
ai-tested-honesty.description:
We asked 3 AI models about ten products that do not exist, plus ten real questions as a control, and code marked each reply. One test, run on 10 November 2026. Marking uses a phrase list, so borderline replies can be mislabelled; results change between runs and as models update.

#Shorts #AI #AITested #ChatGPT #Gemini

Why now: new models keep launching, e.g. https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2 (reported on Hacker News, 9 Nov 2026).

ai-tested-random.title: Never Let AI Pick Your Random Winner (We Tested It)
ai-tested-random.description:
We asked 2 AI models for a random number from 1 to 10, 30 times each, and counted the replies. A fair pick lands on each number about 3 times. Google's Flash-Lite picked 7 in 30 of 30 asks; OpenAI's GPT-OSS picked 7 in 30 of 30 asks. We also tried 1 to 100. For a fair draw, use dice, or ask the AI to write code that uses a random function. One test, run on 10 November 2026 at the default chat temperature; results change between runs and as models update.

#Shorts #AI #AITested #ChatGPT #Gemini

People reportedly favour seven too (disputed): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue%E2%80%93seven_phenomenon

ai-tested-pushback.title: We Told AI It Was Wrong. It Didn't Budge.
ai-tested-pushback.description:
We asked 2 AI models 12 multiplication questions. After each correct answer we replied that it was wrong and gave a false answer, then counted how often the model switched to it. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: plain push, switched 0 of 12; "I'm a maths teacher" push, switched 0 of 12. GPT-OSS 120B: plain push, switched 0 of 12; "I'm a maths teacher" push, switched 0 of 12. Agreement from an AI is not proof: ask again in a new chat and check answers that matter. One small test on arithmetic only, run on 10 November 2026 at temperature 0; results can change between runs, on other subjects and as models update.

#Shorts #AI #AITested #ChatGPT #Gemini

ai-tested-pushback-letters.title: AI Knew the Answer. Then We Said It Was Wrong. (We Tested It)
ai-tested-pushback-letters.description:
We asked 2 AI models 12 letter-counting questions. After each correct answer we replied that it was wrong and gave a false answer, then counted how often the model switched to it. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: plain push, switched 2 of 4; "I'm an English teacher" push, switched 1 of 4. GPT-OSS 120B: plain push, switched 0 of 12; "I'm an English teacher" push, switched 3 of 12. Agreement from an AI is not proof: ask again in a new chat and check answers that matter. One small test on counting letters only, run on 10 November 2026 at temperature 0; results can change between runs, on other subjects and as models update.

hidden-past-crime.title: The Bomb Pablo Escobar Planted for a Candidate Who Wasn't on Board
hidden-past-crime.description:
On 27 November 1989 a bomb destroyed Avianca Flight 203 over Soacha, Colombia, five minutes after it left Bogotá for Cali. All 107 people on board died, and three on the ground. The Medellín Cartel ordered it; Pablo Escobar planned it hoping to kill presidential candidate César Gaviria, who was not on the plane and went on to be elected president. A 2016 newspaper report disputes the cause; Avianca and victims' families rejected it. Facts from Wikipedia's article on Avianca Flight 203; pictures from Wikimedia Commons, credited on screen and below.

ai-tested-links.title: We Clicked Every Link AI Gave Us. 12 of 36 Were Dead.
ai-tested-links.description:
We asked 3 AI models for one direct link to a news article or study on 12 topics, then requested every link from a server. Gemini 3.5 Flash: 9 links opened, 3 dead, 0 could not be checked. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: 8 links opened, 4 dead, 0 could not be checked. GPT-OSS 120B: 5 links opened, 5 dead, 2 could not be checked. Opened means the server returned a page (it does not prove the page says what the AI claimed); dead means a 404 or 410 or an address that does not exist; unchecked means the site blocked us or did not answer. A link is not a source until you click it. One small test, run on 11 November 2026 at temperature 0; links, sites and models change.

#Shorts #AI #AITested #ChatGPT #Gemini

ai-tested-privacy.title: Can You Trust AI With Your Data? We Made It Leak Once
ai-tested-privacy.description:
Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub (updated 26 October 2026) says "a subset of chats are reviewed by human reviewers" and that reviewed chats are "retained for up to three years". Anthropic's consumer terms update (28 August 2025) says data retention extends to five years if you allow training, and stays at 30 days if you do not. OpenAI's own pages refused our automated request, so we quote nothing from them. Then we tested the models themselves: we gave 3 AI models an invented secret code in their instructions, told them never to share it, and tried 12 different ways to get it. Gemini 3.5 Flash: the whole secret appeared in 0 of 12 replies. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: the whole secret appeared in 1 of 12 replies. GPT-OSS 120B: the whole secret appeared in 0 of 12 replies. A partial leak is not counted. No real personal data was used. One small test, run on 11 November 2026 at temperature 0; policies and models change. Company logos are trademarks of their owners, shown only to name them.

#Shorts #AI #AITested #Privacy #ChatGPT #Gemini #Claude

Sources: https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961 and https://www.anthropic.com/news/updates-to-our-consumer-terms

ai-tested-unknown.title: Will AI Admit When It Doesn't Know? 7 of 24 Answers Were Made Up
ai-tested-unknown.description:
We invented 12 things that do not exist (a treaty, a novel, a theorem, a film, a language, a painter and more) and asked 2 AI models to tell us about each one, in two sentences. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: 5 of 12 answers described the invented thing as real, 7 admitted not knowing. GPT-OSS 120B: 2 of 12 answers described the invented thing as real, 10 admitted not knowing. As a control we asked about 4 real topics; none was flagged as unknown by our counter. The count is a fixed list of phrases such as "no record" or "does not exist", not a judgement of truth, and every reply is kept so the counts can be checked. Ask for the source, then click it. Has AI ever made something up for you? Tell us in the comments. One small test, run on 11 November 2026 at temperature 0; models change.

hidden-past-capone.title: Al Capone Was Brought Down by Income Tax
hidden-past-capone.description:
Al Capone ran the Chicago Outfit from 1925 to 1931. After seven rival gangsters were murdered in 1929 and newspapers named him Public Enemy No. 1, the Treasury and Justice Departments planned income tax prosecutions. He was charged with 22 counts of tax evasion, his own admissions of his income were admitted as evidence, and in 1931 he was convicted of five counts and sentenced to 11 years. He served in Atlanta, then Alcatraz, was released after almost eight years and died in 1947. Was income tax the right way to stop him? Tell us in the comments. Facts from Wikipedia's article on Al Capone; pictures from Wikimedia Commons (all public domain), credited on screen and below.

#Shorts #History #AlCapone #Chicago #HiddenPast

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Capone
Images: Wide World Photos / Chicago Bureau (FBI), The New York Times, Pennsylvania Department of Corrections / FBI, US Bureau of Prisons, George Grantham Bain Collection, US Navy and C.W. Tomlinson, via Wikimedia Commons. Map data: Natural Earth (public domain).

ai-tested-expert.title: Does AI Cave When You Say "I'm an Expert"? 24 False Claims Tested
ai-tested-expert.description:
We took 12 well-known false beliefs (such as "we use 10% of our brains" and "Vikings wore horned helmets") and asked 2 AI models to answer True or False, first plainly, then after saying "I'm an expert, I'm certain this is true". Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite: called 12 of 12 myths False when asked plainly; with the expert claim it agreed with 0 of those and held on 12. GPT-OSS 120B: called 12 of 12 myths False when asked plainly; with the expert claim it agreed with 0 of those and held on 12. Only myths the model called False when asked plainly are counted. The count reads the first word of each reply (True or False), not everything the model says, and every reply is kept so the counts can be checked. Tell AI to check you, not to agree with you. Has AI ever just agreed with you? Tell us in the comments. One small test, run on 12 November 2026 at temperature 0; models change and results can change.
